# dsh-deepseek-cost

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that shows what the conversation has cost so far:
a cost pill beside

the built-in step/time and token statistics, with the session
total and the current turn priced at

DeepSeek's official peak/off-peak API rates,
plus one 花费 row in the built-in 本轮用量 panel of every com

pleted turn.
Both of DeepSeek's own routes — the API key and the signed-in account — are
priced; eve
ry other route is counted as `0`.
## What it adds

One **cost pill** in the composer dock, inline beside the built-in step/time and
token pills. The le

ading `¥` is the currency mark for the whole pill, so the
amounts beside it stay bare — one symbol p

er pill — and every figure is shown at
two decimals:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

A route billed at `0` still spent tokens, so the collapsed pill shows what those
calls *would* have

cost at official rates beside the billed figure, in
parentheses and one step dimmer (`--dsw-alias-la

bel-caption`) — otherwise the
pill reads a flat `0.00` for a session that in fact ran elsewhere. Eac

h scope
carries its own estimate, and the parentheses come from the dictionary, so the
English pill

uses ASCII parentheses with a leading space while the Chinese one
uses full-width ones. The accessib

le name spells the estimate out
(`会话花费 ¥ 0.00（预估 ~¥ 0.98）…`) rather than leaving it to the punctuati

name spells the estimate out
(`会话花费 ¥ 0.00（预估 ~¥ 0.98）…`) rather than leaving it to the punctuation.

Two decimals means an amount below half a cent shows as `0.00`. The wire keeps
six decimals and the

host prices exactly, so nothing is lost upstream; it takes a
very short turn with a warm cache to la
nd below the display threshold at all.

Clicking it opens its own details dialog, shaped like the built-in step and token
dialogs: the same

panel material, title, and rule, and the same shipped
`useAnchoredPosition` / `useDismissOnOutsidePo

inter` primitives to position and
dismiss it.

The material is the built-in one token for token, which matters more than it
looks: the menu surface

(`--dsw-specific-menu`) is a *translucent* colour —
`#303136f0` in the desktop dark theme — and it

only reads as solid because the
built-in panels also apply `backdrop-filter: var(--dsw-menu-backdrop

-filter)`
(`blur(40px) saturate(150%)`, defined on `body` and so inherited by a panel
portaled to `b

ody`). A panel that sets the surface without that filter shows the
transcript through it. The radius

is the theme's `--dsw-radius-lg` rather than a
hardcoded value, for the same reason. `client.test.m
js` case 16 pins this.

The panel itself is the grid: the cost category, then **one column per scope**.
[该节后续省略]
## How it works

**Host half** (`lib/index.js`) registers the `deepseekCost` session projection on
`ctx.sessionProjec

tions`. A projection is a pure, synchronous fold over the
whole durable session log, so the figures

are complete regardless of transcript
paging and compaction — the same seam `tokenUsage` and `sessio

regardless of transcript
paging and compaction — the same seam `tokenUsage` and `sessionStats` use.

The fold mirrors token-meter's replacement rule: the last usage sample inside one
`(turn, step)` rep

laces its predecessor, and `llm/retry-started` closes that slot
so a retried attempt adds a second b

illed attempt. Route attribution prefers the
settled assistant message's own `source`, then the last

`request/header` /
`request/context` snapshot.

Besides the session and current-turn totals, the fold keeps a **per-turn ledger**
(`turns`, keyed by

the turn number) of every turn's cost and estimate. A finished
turn is never the current turn again

— `turn/start` resets the current-turn
figures at every boundary — yet its usage panel stays openab

le from the
transcript, so the ledger is what makes that panel answerable. Replacement and
retry rew
rite only their own turn's entry.

**Browser half** (`lib/client.js`) registers one occupant on the
`conversation.composer.dock` list s

lot, reads the projection with
`useProjection('deepseekCost')`, and returns the pill as that occupan

t's element.
The dock is a flex row (`InputBar.module.css` `.dock`), so the pill is laid out
inline

beside the built-in pills; the occupant owns no portal and no anchoring.
The pill owns its dialog se

at, replicating the built-in `useStatDialog` placement
and dismissal from the shipped primitives. Th

e occupant's one effect is the
turn-usage row watcher described above.

The dock slot is the public contract, which is what makes the pill survive DSH
upgrades: 0.1.6 dropp

ed the statistics row's `data-composer-stats` hook that an
inline portal would have needed. The pill

never referenced a class name belonging
to another package. The 本轮用量 row is the deliberate exceptio

n — that panel
offers no slot — and it is confined to the two `data-` attributes above rather
than a
ny hashed class name.
[该节后续省略]
## What the plugin list shows

Settings lists this plugin as **DeepSeek 花费统计** with a one-line summary,
instead of the bare module-

derived `deepseek-cost`. DSH reads that text from
`<package>/locale/<language>.json` — the same mech

anism the shipped packages use —
through the package's own `exports`, so the resource must be export

sm the shipped packages use —
through the package's own `exports`, so the resource must be exported:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- The filename is the language id (`en.json`, `zh.json`, …), the key inside is
`meta`, and **`en.jso

n` is required**: DSH enumerates that directory only when
the English resource resolves, and `ctx.lo

cale.resolveText` needs the `en`
fallback before it walks the active language's fallback chain (`zh-

CN` → `zh` →
`en`).
- `package.json` `name` / `description` remain the fallbacks for a package with

no
locale directory, and the plugin list shortens a bare `name` by stripping the
`dsh-` / `dsh-host-

` / `dsh-client-` prefix — which is why the plugin used to
read `deepseek-cost`.
- `package.json` `i

con` (a manifest-relative SVG/PNG/JPEG/WebP under 256 KiB) is
read the same way. This package ships
